title: Sable and the Asset
premise: Edmund Yarrow, a private security contractor who has spent three years erasing himself from every database, guards a reclusive client whose encrypted servers should be untouchable. When a routine voiceprint check unlocks a server in Lisbon, Edmund discovers his own voice was the key — evidence that he was once an asset in a program he cannot remember, and that his client has been studying him for years. As rival contractors close in to silence everyone connected to the program, Edmund must decide whether to trade the recovered memory files — the only proof of what was done to him and others — or destroy them to protect the few people he's come to care about. In the end, he leaks a partial archive, burns his old identity for good, and walks away knowing that belonging was never something he lost, but something he finally chooses.
about_author: Hazel Vasquez is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments before turning to fiction. She lives off-grid by choice and writes her thrillers on paper first, distrusting anything with a microphone.

chapters.title: The Quiet Client
chapters.summary: POV Edmund Yarrow. Edmund runs security protocols at a remote estate for a client known only as Meridian, cataloguing the small rituals of invisibility that keep them both safe. The beat is controlled unease: Edmund is competent but hollow, aware that his anonymity is both armor and prison.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. New operating orders arrive with no sender, changing access hierarchies overnight. Edmund's colleague Dana teases him about paranoia; he can't explain why the changes feel personal. Beat: creeping suspicion as the ground shifts beneath professional habit.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A scheduled biometric audit requires Edmund to speak a passphrase into the estate's system. Somewhere across the Atlantic, a server in Lisbon answers — unlocked not by the client's credentials, but by his voice. Beat: cold shock, the first crack in three years of safety.

chapters.title: What the Server Knew
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with intercepted documents rendered as fragments. The Lisbon server contains personnel files from a defunct program called SABLE — and one file carries Edmund's face under a different name. Beat: vertigo of self-estrangement; memory becomes unreliable terrain.

chapters.title: Dana's Questions
chapters.summary: POV Dana Reyes, Edmund's junior colleague. She notices Edmund pulling archived logs at 3 a.m. and covers for him during a surprise inspection, then demands answers. Beat: loyalty tested early; Dana chooses trust over protocol, deepening their bond.

chapters.title: Meridian's Study
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund breaks into the client's private study and finds years of surveillance reports — on himself. His client has been documenting his dreams, his habits, his gaps in memory. Beat: betrayal sharpened by the realization that someone watched him grieve without knowing why.

chapters.title: The Man from Rotterdam
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A 'vendor' arrives for a scheduled maintenance visit and asks questions no vendor would ask. Edmund feeds him false answers while quietly confirming the man is contract muscle for whoever owns SABLE's remnants. Beat: hunter and hunted circling in polite conversation.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Personal Size
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Dana discovers her own background file has been flagged and altered — she's being positioned as a scapegoat. She confronts Edmund, who must decide how much truth to share. Beat: guilt and confession; Edmund tells her about SABLE, sealing them together.

chapters.title: Lisbon Calling
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Following the server trail, Edmund contacts a former handler, Ilse Brandt, now living quietly in Portugal. She confirms SABLE existed — and warns him that the memories were removed for a reason. Beat: temptation of knowledge versus terror of what it holds.

chapters.title: Half a Life
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Ilse gives him a partial decryption key and a warning: the full archive includes names of other subjects, some still alive, all still watched. Edmund experiences his first sensory flashback — rain, a runway, a woman saying his real name. Beat: grief arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: The Estate Locks Down
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Communications go dark; the estate shifts to lockdown protocols nobody authorized. Dana realizes the maintenance visit was reconnaissance and the real operation begins tonight. Beat: rising dread, the thriller engine engaging.

chapters.title: Meridian Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. His client finally reveals herself: a former SABLE architect who claims she took Edmund in to protect him from the people cleaning up the program. She offers him the full key — if he surrenders the archive to her, not the world. Beat: seductive ambiguity; protector or captor?

chapters.title: Night Visitors
chapters.summary: POV Edmund and alternating Dana. The cleanup team breaches the estate. Edmund and Dana execute escape routes he designed for clients, never for himself. Beat: adrenaline and competence under fire; the invisible man becomes visible exactly when it costs most.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Hiding in a coastal safehouse, they count assets: one partial key, one ally abroad, maybe forty hours before trackers converge. Dana challenges Edmund's plan to trade the archive instead of publishing it. Beat: loyalty versus truth made explicit between friends.

chapters.title: Ilse's Price
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In Lisbon, Ilse agrees to complete the decryption but reveals her own stake: her brother was a SABLE subject who died confused and erased. She wants the whole archive public, whatever it does to Edmund. Beat: moral pressure mounting from every direction.

chapters.title: The Runway Memory
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Under Ilse's guidance, the decryption triggers a full flashback: Edmund volunteered, then tried to walk out, then chose erasure over testifying against colleagues he loved. Beat: devastating clarity — he didn't lose his past; he sentenced himself to forget it.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Meridian's people offer the exchange: the complete key for the archive, plus new identities for Edmund and Dana. Edmund stalls, buying time while Ilse mirrors the files. Beat: the con within the negotiation; Edmund finally plays offense.

chapters.title: Handover
chapters.summary: POV Edmund and Dana. The exchange happens in a decommissioned ferry terminal. It proceeds cleanly — too cleanly — until Edmund realizes Meridian intended to take Dana as leverage regardless. Beat: betrayal confirmed; the trap springs and fails by inches.

chapters.title: Sable Rising
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Cornered in the terminal's lower decks, Edmund fights through the cleanup team using skills he didn't know he had — SABLE training surfacing like scar tissue. He reaches the broadcast uplink with seconds left. Beat: climax; the past weaponized in service of truth.

chapters.title: Everything at Once
chapters.summary: POV multiple, brief intercuts. The partial archive goes live: names, methods, victims. Meridian escapes rather than be named; Ilse watches her brother's file finally read by strangers; Dana shields Edmund from the last shooter. Beat: catharsis amid chaos; truth costs everything except itself.

chapters.title: Afterimages
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Weeks later, investigations bloom and denials circulate. Dana recovers in a rented house by the sea, angry that justice arrived diluted, grateful Edmund kept his promise about her name staying out of the leak. Beat: bruised tenderness; loyalty survived the truth.

chapters.title: A Name He Chooses
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund visits the runway from his memory, leaves flowers for the woman who spoke his name, then deletes the last backup of his old identity himself. He takes a small contract guarding a family that knows his face. Beat: resolution — belonging rebuilt deliberately, memory carried instead of feared.
